title: Octanol-induced head shapes are morphometrically closer to the species they resemble

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Octanol-induced head shapes are morphometrically closer to the species they resemble

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: By geometric morphometrics (Procrustes distances), the octanol-induced head shapes of G. dorotocephala regenerates are closer to the wild-type head shapes of the species they resemble than to the wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.2. Quantitative Comparison of Induced vs. Genome-Specific Head Shapes

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Comparisons of the Procrustes distances between shape groups (Figure 2A, Table 1) showed that the experimentally derived morphologies were closer in shape to the wild-type morphologies they resembled than the wild-type Girardia dorotocephala head morphology.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.2. Quantitative Comparison of Induced vs. Genome-Specific Head Shapes”. Scope: Landmark-based head shapes of octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates and wild-type G. dorotocephala, D. japonica, S. mediterranea and P. felina

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The metric and criterion are explicit and published measurements permit partial checking. Lack of a clearly deposited raw coordinate matrix and possible classification circularity prevent a fully independent resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the published landmarks to all specimen images, perform Procrustes alignment, and compare each pseudo group with wild-type reference groups. Support requires smaller distance to the resembled species than to G. dorotocephala with uncertainty estimates.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Groups were assigned partly from the morphology being tested.

The complete landmark coordinate matrix is not clearly available.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The comparison is a standard morphometric inequality, and the distance table is published with sample sizes. A reader can check the reported ordering and the published ANOVA. Without the landmarks, placement, semi-landmark sliding, and the circularity of assigning groups by eye stay unauditable, so the table supports only a partial check.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute Procrustes distances among the published groups, or, if raw landmarks become available, recompute them from the stated landmarks. Distances from each induced group to its reference species smaller than distances to wild-type Girardia would support the claim; the opposite ordering would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Groups were predefined by the resemblance the distances are then used to demonstrate.

Raw landmark coordinates are not deposited, so distances cannot be recomputed from images.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In the published Procrustes distances between head-shape groups, each octanol-induced G. dorotocephala head-shape group is closer to the wild-type head shape of the species it resembles than to the wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py downloads the paper's Europe PMC full-text XML, parses Table 1 into a symmetric distance matrix (keeping which cells are bold) and, for each pseudo group (D. japonica-, P. felina- and S. mediterranea-like), compares its distance to the resembled species' wild type with its distance to wild-type G. dorotocephala. As a secondary measure, not part of the verdict, it lists each pseudo group's nearest wild-type group among all five wild-type groups, including G. dorotocephala regenerated for 10 days in water.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: for every induced group in the published table (e.g. D. japonica-like, S. mediterranea-like, P. felina-like), the Procrustes distance to the resembled species' wild type is smaller than its distance to wild-type G. dorotocephala; if the table also reports significance of between-group distances (permutation p-values), the induced-vs-G. dorotocephala distance is significant (p < 0.05) for every induced group.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: at most one of the induced groups (or, with two groups, neither) is closer to its resembled species than to wild-type G. dorotocephala. If all are closer by distance but a reported significance test fails for some group, or exactly one of three groups violates the ordering, the verdict is 'mixed'. If no distance table can be retrieved, 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: of 3 octanol-induced pseudo-species groups closer (Procrustes distance) to the resembled species' wild type than to wild-type G. dorotocephala

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: published distances to two decimals; no dispersion or per-pair test reported in the table

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: The claim is tested exactly as an inequality on the published Procrustes distance table: for each induced group, d(induced, resembled species) < d(induced, G. dorotocephala). Raw landmark coordinates are not deposited, so the distances cannot be recomputed from specimens; this is an audit of the source paper's own measurements, not an independent test. Group membership of the induced animals was assigned by eye from the same morphology that is then measured, which the test cannot remove.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Emmons-Bell et al. 2015, Int J Mol Sci 16:27865-27896, Table 1: Procrustes distances between head-shape groups (Europe PMC full text XML, PMC4661923)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The literal inequality holds for all three groups (D. japonica-like 0.14 vs 0.19, P. felina-like 0.09 vs 0.40, S. mediterranea-like 0.22 vs 0.25), so the pre-registered rule gives 'supports'. The table reports no dispersion and no per-pair significance test, so the significance clause of the pass criterion could not be applied; the only reported tests are ANOVAs across all groups (centroid size F = 7.94, shape F = 7.40, both p < 0.0001).

Two of the three margins are small (0.05 and 0.03 Procrustes units) relative to the distance between intact and regenerated wild-type G. dorotocephala (0.10), and the groups have only 5-13 animals.

Outside the verdict, the full matrix weakens the 'species-specific' reading. Only the P. felina-like group is nearest its resembled species. The D. japonica-like group is as close to G. dorotocephala regenerated in water (0.14) as to D. japonica (0.14), and regenerated G. dorotocephala is arguably the right control for regenerates. The S. mediterranea-like group is nearer wild-type D. japonica (0.17) and the D. japonica-like group (0.09) than wild-type S. mediterranea (0.22).

Not independent: this audits the source paper's own table. Raw landmarks are not deposited, so the distances cannot be recomputed, and induced animals were assigned to groups by eye from the same head shape that is then measured, which biases each group toward its label.

The table footnote abbreviates P. felina as 'P. feline'; the analysis follows the table's group labels.
